# Results — Study 73 (First-Light) on real 5-minute tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — the 5-minute
Opening Range Breakout (ORB) on RTH 5-minute bars: define the opening range as the first
5-minute bar (09:30–09:35 ET); go **long** when a later bar closes above the range high,
**short** when it closes below the range low; hold with a stop of 1× range-size and exit
flat at the 16:00 close. Tested across SPY, QQQ, IWM, TQQQ (~60 days, ~1 signal/day),
with a **random-direction control** on identical entries. As-of **2026-06-12**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| SPY  | 2026-03-19 → 2026-06-12 | `0b838391fc70` |

*Yahoo serves at most ~60 calendar days of 5-minute bars; this is the structural power
ceiling of the study, not a bug.*

## The honest test — 5-min ORB, exit at close (no TP), stop = 1× range, gross

Each session produces exactly one signal: the first bar to close outside the 09:30 opening
bar. The exit is end-of-day (flat at 16:00) unless the stop is hit first. Pooled across
four tickers: **n = 240 trades** (~1 signal/ticker/day).

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **ORB (breakout direction)** | 240 | **31.7%** | **+2.18** | +3.72 | **+0.40** |
| Random direction (control) | 240 | 28.3% | −0.67 | — | −0.10 |

- The ORB's gross expectancy is **+2.18 bps/trade** at HAC *t* = **+0.40** — well below the
  inference bar of |*t*| ≥ 2. The pooled bootstrap 95% CI on the annualised Sharpe is
  **[−1.26, +1.67]** (31% of resamples negative).
- The ORB does *beat* the random coin by **+2.85 bps**, but the gap is entirely
  statistically insignificant. This is consistent with a small genuine effect that the
  60-day window has no power to confirm.
- **Win-rate is only ~32%**: the exit-at-close variant captures large moves when the
  breakout runs but stops out at 1× range-size frequently. The positive skew (+3.72)
  reflects a few large winners — the opposite of the fixed-tick win-rate illusion.

### Per-instrument breakdown

| Ticker | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 60 | 26.7% | −0.16 | −0.03 |
| QQQ  | 60 | 31.7% | −0.25 | −0.04 |
| IWM  | 60 | 38.3% | +9.41 | +1.04 |
| TQQQ | 60 | 30.0% | −0.27 | −0.01 |

The pooled positive mean is almost entirely driven by IWM (HAC *t* = +1.04 — suggestive
but not significant in isolation). SPY, QQQ, TQQQ each post negligible, slightly negative
results. No ticker clears |*t*| ≥ 2.

## 15-minute ORB (range_bars = 3)

Using the first three 5-minute bars (09:30–09:45) as the opening range:

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **15-min ORB** | 240 | **37.5%** | **+2.54** | **+0.41** |
| Random direction | 240 | 37.9% | −0.56 | −0.08 |

Slightly larger mean (+2.54 bps) but still HAC *t* = +0.41. The wider opening range does
not materially improve inference; both variants are below the bar.

## Cost sweep — 5-min ORB, net

At ~1 trade/ticker/day the turnover is modest compared with the SMA scalp, but the thin
gross edge (~+2 bps) is extinguished quickly:

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +2.18 | +0.40 |
| 0.5 bps | +1.68 | +0.31 |
| 1.0 bps | +1.18 | +0.22 |
| 2.0 bps | +0.18 | +0.03 |
| 5.0 bps | −2.82 | −0.52 |

The signal vanishes into noise by ~1–2 bps. At realistic broker costs for 5-minute
intraday trading (spread ≈ 0.5–2 bps depending on product) the expected net gain is
near zero and statistically indistinguishable from noise. There is no confident loser
here either — unlike the SMA scalp, the ORB does not *certify* as a significant loser,
it simply fails to certify as a winner.

## TQQQ leverage drag — the Zarattini & Aiolfi (2023) version

The paper's most headline-grabbing claim involves 3×-leveraged TQQQ. Even ignoring the
signal question, a TQQQ ORB carries daily financing drag from the leverage:

| TQQQ financing drag | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps/day (no drag, naive) | −1.27 | −0.06 | 30.0% |
| 25 bps/day (half estimate) | −11.19 | −0.56 | 28.3% |
| 50 bps/day (realistic estimate) | −21.11 | −1.10 | 26.7% |

The TQQQ ORB is already slightly negative before drag; the realistic ~50 bps/day
leverage cost (3× product expense ratios + implicit financing at current T-bill rates)
turns it into a significant hole. The amplifier works on both directions.

## Synthetic positive control

The ORB engine correctly recovers an edge on the synthetic tape when an opening-range
drift is planted, and reads ≈ 0 on a fair open — confirming the machine is working and
the real-tape verdict is a statement about the market, not the method:

| Planted session-start drift | ORB gross (bps/trade) | beats random? |
|---|--:|:--:|
| 0 bps (fair open) | ≈ 0 (coin) | no |
| +20 bps (moderate drift) | positive | yes |
| −20 bps (opening reversal) | negative | no (wrong side) |

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Gross pooled mean +2.18 bps/trade, HAC *t* = +0.40 — positive but
  far below |*t*| ≥ 2. Bootstrap 95% CI on Sharpe spans from −1.26 to +1.67.  The IWM
  result (t = +1.04) is the strongest single instrument but still not significant.  The
  signal is WEAK: directionally correct but unconfirmed in 60 days of data.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The thin gross edge (+2.18 bps) is fully absorbed by ~1 bp of
  round-trip cost; at 2 bps the net is +0.18 bps (noise). The TQQQ version adds
  substantial leverage-financing drag that turns it clearly negative.
- **Beats a coin? — NOT CONFIRMED.** The ORB scores +2.85 bps above a random-direction
  control, but the difference is statistically invisible (n=240, 60-day window). Literature
  support (Zarattini & Aiolfi 2023) is real but the claimed returns rely on leverage and
  unrealistic cost assumptions.
